newsitem.title: FRANCE: Algeria council looks at draft budget for 1997.
newsitem.headline: Algeria council looks at draft budget for 1997.

text.p: Algeria's draft budget, adopted last month by the cabinet and which forecasts a surplus of 0.3 percent of Gross Domestic Product, goes to the National Transitional Council (CNT) on Wednesday for discussion.

The official Algerian news agency APS said the draft budget envisaged, for the first time since independence from France in 1962, repayment of part of the public debt. The repayment would total 35 billion dinars ($648.1 million), it said.
The CNT is an unelected quasi-parliament, appointed by the authorities in the absence of an elected assembly and usually accepts government recommendations.
APS said the budget had been drawn up on the basis of income from oil sales at $17.5 per barrel for 1997, compared with $16.5 per barrel for 1996.
OPEC member, Algeria earns some 95 percent of its foreign income from its energy sales.
More than 100 billion dinars of the budget is to be devoted to modernising Algeria's industry, according to Prime Minister Ahmed Ouyahia, APS said.
Algeria's industry outside the oil and gas sector has been crippled by lack of spares, poor management, and shortages of raw materials.

Officials have said that most of some 400 state enterprises outside the energy sector are inefficient, operating often at only up to 50 percent capacity. The treasury has already pumped 500 billion dinars into them over seven years.
Despite this, industrial output in the first six months of this year fell seven percent, earning just $366 million in exports, against the same period last year.
APS gave no other figures for the budget but President Liamine Zeroual said last month that there would be an increase in social spending for the poorest members of Algeria's 29 million population.
Algerian authorities have been engaged in a five-year-old conflict with Moslem fundamentalists whose ranks, according to officials, have been reinforced by young people affected by poverty.
